messages:
marie: Heads up — we're seeing repeated preemptible GPU evictions in europe-west1 that are triggering cross-zone on-demand provisioning and then a cascade of SNAT exhaustion on the egress NATs. First spike ~ 2034567800, still happening.

marie: Alert screenshot from infra-dash: autoscaler up from 40 -> 95 nodes in 3 mins, then lots of node drains. Metrics: GPU utilization dropped while CPU pods spilled to on-demand. :frown:

autoscaler-bot: [alert] cluster-autoscaler: scale up triggered by unschedulable pods (gpu-workloads), new nodes requested: 55, zones: eu-west1-b,c,a.

devon: Can you paste the CA logs? Also, which nodepools are affected (preemptible vs on-demand)?

marie: CA logs (excerpt):
```
I0321 18:12:41.123456 1 scale_up.go:123] Pod default/realtime-infer-abc is unschedulable, requesting 1 gpu node from nodegroup gpu-preemptible-eu
I0321 18:12:42.789012 1 scale_up.go:210] Scale-up: adding 55 nodes to nodegroup gpu-preemptible-eu (max 100)
I0321 18:13:01.001100 1 balance.go:88] Rebalance: moving pods, considering removing nodes in eu-west1-b
I0321 18:13:05.445500 1 scale_up.go:300] Fallback: requesting 40 on-demand nodes from nodegroup gpu-on-demand-eu
```

marie: Node pool layout: gpu-preemptible-eu (preemptible, mixed zones), gpu-on-demand-eu (on-demand, same zones), warm-standby-eu (tainted, kept at ~5).

lee: Sounds like CA is deciding to fallback to on-demand in other zones rather than using warm-standby in the same AZ. Could be the balancing heuristic + pod topology constraints.

santiago: Also, when many nodes drain simultaneously we blast the NAT gateway because each drained pod does egress cloning during image pulls / checkpoints. We saw SNAT port exhaustion logs on nat-ops.

devon: Short-term mitigation options: 1) Temporarily set gpu-on-demand-eu max surge to 0 (prevent cross-zone provisioning), 2) increase warm-standby to cover delta, 3) disable inter-zone rebalance in CA flags and increase scale up delay. Any objections?

oncall: +1 to warming more standby, but we need to estimate cost impact.

marie: Cost estimate: if we keep 50 extra on-demand GPUs for 2 hours that's ~ $3k-4k (rough). If we let CA keep launching then sustained on-demand could be way higher.

devon: Proposed quick fixes (apply now):
- patch ClusterAutoscaler: set --balance-similar-node-groups=false and --max-node-provision-time=10m
- in GKE nodepools, add taint to gpu-on-demand-eu: spot-fallback=true:NoSchedule and only allow critical fallback via tolerations in rollout job
- scale warm-standby-eu from 5 -> 30 (same AZ preference)

santiago: Also add a temporary drain parallelism throttle to limit concurrent drains: kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30 --timeout=10m and run in batches of 5 nodes.

lee: We should also flip the node-termination-handler to do quicker graceful eviction and KV cache persistence so pods reschedule faster onto warm nodes rather than spilling to other zones.

marie: Example nodepool patch for warm-standby (gcloud):
```
gcloud container node-pools update warm-standby-eu \
  --cluster=prod-eu \
  --num-nodes=30 \
  --node-taints=preemptible-standby=true:NoSchedule
```

devon: Ops plan: (A) apply CA flag change, (B) scale warm-standby to 30, (C) add toleration to the autoscaler-managed fallback job, (D) run controlled drains. I can own A+B, marco can do C, oncall run D. Rollback: revert to previous warm size and CA flags.

marie: +1. I'll open a quick runbook in `#incidents` and notify billing if we hit >$5k.

autoscaler-bot: [info] applied flag update: --balance-similar-node-groups=false by devon at 18:40

devon: I patched warm-standby to 30. Monitoring CPU/GPU spread now.

santiago: NAT port graph already looked better after throttling drains. We'll keep an eye for 15m.

lee: Post-mortem actions we should track: replace blind fallback with zone-local fallback, add locality-aware fallback policy in infra-runner, add autoscaler integration test simulating wave evictions, and increase NAT capacity or use multiple NATs per subnet.

marie: Add one more item: consider on-prem warm cache layer to reduce image-pull egress during mass drains (would cut NAT load).

oncall: Thanks team. If we still see evictions after 30m, escalate to pager and start cross-region throttling. :lock:
